title: Common maximal speed: two body types recorded by one medium

key_results.statement: All replacements leaving $C$ unchanged: $t'^A_{hh}=t^A_{hh}+\alpha^A_h$, $K'^A_h=K^A_h+Z-\alpha^A_h\mathbb 1_c$, $t'^B_{kk}=t^B_{kk}+\alpha^B_k$, $K'^B_k=K^B_k-Z-\alpha^B_k\mathbb 1_c$, with real $\alpha^A_h$, $\alpha^B_k$ and self-adjoint $Z$ arbitrary; the parametrization by $(\alpha^A,\alpha^B,Z)$ is one-to-one.

Under (8.1): $\bar x_a\mapsto\bar x_a+z$, $\bar x_b\mapsto\bar x_b-z$ with $z=(Z-\langle Z\rangle)\chi\in\mathcal N$, while $v_a$, $v_b$, $v^A_{\max}$, $v^B_{\max}$ are unchanged; under $\chi\mapsto e^{i\theta}\chi$: $\bar x_a,\bar x_b,v_a,v_b$ are multiplied by $e^{i\theta}$ and $v^A_{\max}$, $v^B_{\max}$ are unchanged.

Well defined: $\lVert v_a\rVert$, $\lVert v_b\rVert$, $g(v_a,v_b)$, $\lVert v_a-v_b\rVert$, $v^A_{\max}$, $v^B_{\max}$ and $v^A_{\max}/v^B_{\max}$ (if $v^B_{\max}>0$); not well defined: $\bar x_a-\bar x_b$, neither the vector nor its norm.
Exactly, $\lVert v_a(\lambda)\rVert\le\sum_{h,h'}a^A_{hh'}q_hq_{h'}\le v^A_{\max}$ for every product start and every $\lambda\in\mathbb R$, in the presence of body $b$; likewise for $b$.

$a^A_{hh'}=\lvert t^A_{hh'}\rvert\,\lVert(K^A_h-K^A_{h'}-\langle K^A_h-K^A_{h'}\rangle)\chi\rVert$, so $v^A_{\max}$ depends only on the off-diagonal $t^A$, the differences of the $K^A_h$ and $\chi$, not on $C_B$, $K^B_k$ or $\vartheta$.

Exactly, $v^T_{\max}=2\eta_Td_1^T\cos\frac{\pi}{L_T+1}\to2\eta_Td_1^T$ for $L_T\to\infty$: $2t_T\sigma_{X_T}$ for a chain type and $\tau_T\kappa_T\sigma_{X_T}$ for a Model D type, independent of $m_T$, $N_T$, $\lambda_{0T}$.

Exactly, for chains on $\mathbb Z$ and for finite chains with $L_A=L_B\ge2$: $v^A_{\max}=v^B_{\max}$ iff $t_A\sigma_{X_A}=t_B\sigma_{X_B}$ for chain types, and iff $\tau_A\kappa_A\sigma_{X_A}=\tau_B\kappa_B\sigma_{X_B}$ for Model D types; for finite chains in general iff $\eta_Ad_1^A\cos\frac{\pi}{L_A+1}=\eta_Bd_1^B\cos\frac{\pi}{L_B+1}$.
Laws 1-5 and A1-A9 do not imply $v^A_{\max}=v^B_{\max}$: admissible chain descriptions realize every ratio $v^A_{\max}/v^B_{\max}=t_A\sigma_{X_A}/(t_B\sigma_{X_B})\in(0,\infty)$.

For two chains or two Model D types with the same number $L\ge2$ of positions, a correspondence of all points exists iff $\ell_B=\pm\ell_A$, which implies $d_1^A=d_1^B$; then $v^A_{\max}=v^B_{\max}$ iff $\eta_A=\eta_B$, that is $t_A=t_B$ for chains and $\tau_A=\tau_B$ for Model D.

For two Model D types in the weak-record regime, $\lvert\Psi(\lambda)\rangle=e^{-iC^{\rm D}_A\lambda}\lvert\phi\rangle\otimes e^{-iC^{\rm D}_B\lambda}\lvert\vartheta\rangle\otimes\lvert\chi\rangle+O(\kappa_A)+O(\kappa_B)$ with $C^{\rm D}_T$ the displayed Model D contract and the remainder bounded by (8.23), so the view of each body is that of its own body contract alone and the one-body results of 05 and 06 apply to each body.

Effective body contracts: $C^{\rm eff}_A\otimes\mathbb 1_b+\mathbb 1_a\otimes C^{\rm eff}_B:=(\mathbb 1_{ab}\otimes\langle\chi\rvert)C(\mathbb 1_{ab}\otimes\lvert\chi\rangle)$, that is $C^{\rm eff}_A=C_A+\sum_h\langle K^A_h\rangle\lvert h\rangle\langle h\rvert$ and $C^{\rm eff}_B=C_B+\sum_k\langle K^B_k\rangle\lvert k\rangle\langle k\rvert$.

Under the whole family (8.1), $C^{\rm eff}_A\mapsto C^{\rm eff}_A+\langle Z\rangle\mathbb 1_a$ and $C^{\rm eff}_B\mapsto C^{\rm eff}_B-\langle Z\rangle\mathbb 1_b$, and both are unchanged by the phase of $\chi$; eigenvectors and eigenvalue differences of $C^{\rm eff}_T$ are well defined, single eigenvalues of $C^{\rm eff}_T$ are not, and neither are the eigenvalues and the spectral width of a displayed $C_T$ with at least two places.

Exactly, for every description of item 1, every product start and $\lambda\ge0$: $\lVert\Psi(\lambda)-\phi(\lambda)\otimes\vartheta(\lambda)\otimes\chi\rVert\le\varsigma(\lambda):=\int_0^\lambda(\sum_{h,k}\lvert\phi_h(s)\rvert^2\lvert\vartheta_k(s)\rvert^2\lVert u^A_h+u^B_k\rVert^2)^{1/2}\mathrm ds$ with $\phi(s)=e^{-iC^{\rm eff}_As}\phi$, $\vartheta(s)=e^{-iC^{\rm eff}_Bs}\vartheta$, and $\lVert V_a(\lambda)-\lvert\phi(\lambda)\rangle\langle\phi(\lambda)\rvert\rVert_1\le2\varsigma(\lambda)$; $\varsigma$ is invariant under (8.1).

For a Model D type, in every description of the family (8.1): $C^{\rm eff}_T=C^{\rm D}_T+\gamma_T\hat x_T+c_T\mathbb 1$ with the uniform cost gradient $\gamma_T=\kappa_T\langle X_T\rangle$ and $c_A=-c_B=\langle Z\rangle$.

Exactly, at every finite size: $\varsigma(\lambda)\le\sum_Td_1^T\Lambda_T(\lambda)$ and $\lVert\Psi(\lambda)-e^{-iC^{\rm D}_A\lambda}\phi\otimes e^{-iC^{\rm D}_B\lambda}\vartheta\otimes\chi\rVert\le\sum_T(d_1^T+\lvert\gamma_T\rvert)\Lambda_T(\lambda)$ with $\Lambda_T(\lambda)=\lambda\lVert\hat x_T\phi_T\rVert+\frac12\tau_T\lambda^2$; the right sides contain the chain lengths only through the position moments $\lVert\hat x_T\phi_T\rVert$, so the bounds are uniform in the chain lengths for starts whose position moments are bounded uniformly.

On $\mathbb Z$, a start with plane-wave amplitudes $e^{-ipx^0_T}\delta p_T^{-1/2}f((p-p_{0T})/\delta p_T)\,\xi_T(p)$, with a fixed envelope $f$ of compact support ($\int\lvert f\rvert^2=1$, $\int\lvert f'\rvert^2<\infty$) and a unit internal vector with $\lVert\mathrm d\xi_T/\mathrm dp\rVert\le c_\xi$, has the position moment $\lVert\hat x_T\phi_T\rVert\le\lvert x^0_T\rvert+\lVert f'\rVert_{L^2}/\delta p_T+c_\xi$; concentration near a plane-wave label alone does not bound the position moment.

For equal drift speeds $\nu=\lVert\bar v_a\rVert=\lVert\bar v_b\rVert$: $R_A-R_B=\frac{\nu^2}{2}\bigl[(v^A_{\max})^{-2}-(v^B_{\max})^{-2}\bigr]+O(p_{0A}^4)+O(p_{0B}^4)$, at first order in $\epsilon_T$ and leading order in $\delta p_T$, $\kappa_A$, $\kappa_B$.

To second order in the plane-wave labels the tick ratio is the same function of the drift speed for both types iff $v^A_{\max}=v^B_{\max}$, that is iff $\tau_A\kappa_A\sigma_{X_A}=\tau_B\kappa_B\sigma_{X_B}$.

With the label eliminated, (5.29) reads $R_T^2(1-\beta_T^2)=1+(R_T^2-1)^2/\rho_T^2$, hence on the small-label branch $R_T=1+\frac{\beta_T^2}{2}+\bigl(\frac38+\frac{1}{2\rho_T^2}\bigr)\beta_T^4+O(\beta_T^6)$ with $\beta_T=\nu/v^T_{\max}$, $\rho_T=\tau_T/\bar\mu_T$.

Under $v^A_{\max}=v^B_{\max}$: $R_A-R_B=\frac{\beta^4}{2}\bigl(\bar\mu_A^2/\tau_A^2-\bar\mu_B^2/\tau_B^2\bigr)+O(\beta^6)$; the relations (5.29) of the two types agree iff in addition $\bar\mu_A/\tau_A=\bar\mu_B/\tau_B$ (fixed up to relative terms $O((N_T\epsilon_T)^2)$), so they do not agree in general.

For each type and each clock level, $I^T_k=M^T_k/(v^T_{\max})^2$ with $M^T_k=m_T+\frac{2\pi k}{N_T\lambda_{0T}}$; with $M^T_k=\Delta^T_k/2$ this holds in every description of the family (8.1); with $M^T_k$ read as the positive rest eigenvalue of a body contract it holds in a description iff that eigenvalue equals $M^T_k$ there, which is the case in the displayed Model D description (a sufficient booking, not a necessary one) and for the effective body contract iff $\langle Z\rangle=0$.

On the plane wave with label $0$ and clock level $k$ the translation-invariant part of $C^{\rm eff}_T$ has the eigenvalues $E^T_{k,\pm}=c_T\pm M^T_k$ with $c_A=-c_B=\langle Z\rangle$ arbitrary; the branch gap $\Delta^T_k=2M^T_k$, level differences and $E^A_{k,+}+E^B_{k',+}$ are well defined, the rest cost $E^T_{k,+}$ is not.

Convention-independent relations: $\Delta^T_k=2I^T_k(v^T_{\max})^2$ and $E^T_{k,+}-E^T_{k',+}=(I^T_k-I^T_{k'})(v^T_{\max})^2$; the rest cost itself obeys the affine relation $E^T_{k,+}=c_T+I^T_k(v^T_{\max})^2$ with a conventional intercept $c_T$.

With $M^T_k=\Delta^T_k/2$, the relation between background inertia and rest cost is the same for both types, $M^A_k/I^A_k=M^B_{k'}/I^B_{k'}$ for all levels, iff $v^A_{\max}=v^B_{\max}$, that is iff $\tau_A\kappa_A\sigma_{X_A}=\tau_B\kappa_B\sigma_{X_B}$.

In every description of the family (8.1): $\Delta^A_k/I^A_k=\Delta^B_{k'}/I^B_{k'}$ for all levels, equivalently (for $N_A,N_B\ge2$) equal slopes of rest cost against background inertia, iff $v^A_{\max}=v^B_{\max}$; the affine relations coincide iff in addition $\langle Z\rangle=0$, which is a convention.

The condition (8.13) for a common leading-order tick-ratio law and the conditions (8.17), (8.26) for a common relation between background inertia and rest cost are all equivalent to $v^A_{\max}=v^B_{\max}$.

open_issues: Equality of the maximal speeds is a condition on the description (8.9); nothing in this package selects it (out of scope).

The rest cost as a cost is not well defined; well defined are the branch gap, cost differences within a type and the total of the two bodies (8.24); a later package that needs E = I v_max² as a proportionality must state the booking ⟨Z⟩ = 0 as a convention, and nothing in this setting singles it out.

The quoted inputs do not say whether the starts of 05-moving-clock and 06-inertia-internal-energy have a position moment bounded uniformly in the chain length; item 3 holds for every start in the order κ_T → 0 before L_T → ∞, and the reverse order is justified here only for starts with a uniformly bounded position moment, for example those of (8.27).

The gradient γ_T = κ_T⟨X_T⟩ of (8.22) is convention-independent and of the same order in κ_T as the force on the position label of 06; it does not enter the coefficient of F and its effect on the views is bounded by (8.23), but for ⟨X_T⟩ ≠ 0 it should add an F-independent mean acceleration of order κ_T² that the quoted results do not describe; whether 06 accounts for it cannot be checked from the quoted inputs.
Item 3 inherits the orders of 05-moving-clock and 06-inertia-internal-energy; beyond leading order in κ (out of scope) the influence of b on the view of a is of order κ_A κ_B.
The maximal speed of a type is an upper bound; the drift speeds (5.25) of Model D do not exceed v_top < v_max, which depends on ρ_T as well, so equal v_max does not give equal v_top (8.15).
Chain types and Model D types are compared, as the question asks; for all other types this package gives the general statements (8.1)-(8.6), (8.9) and (8.19)-(8.21), and no closed form.

consistency_checks.check: Dimensions with record vectors as costs (v_max, ς, β, ρ, R, I_k, (8.25)), and invariance of all results and bounds under the rescaling κ_T → sκ_T, X_T → X_T/s that leaves the records unchanged

The rebookings of the two verification rounds as special cases: α = δσ₃ on body A leaves the effective body contract, the branch gap and (8.25) unchanged although the half-gap of the displayed contract changes; the constant shift α^A = c, α^B = −c, Z = c shifts the rest eigenvalues by ±c and leaves gaps, level differences and their sum unchanged; α = δ on the branch s = 2 only, with 0 < δ < m_A, keeps the positive eigenvalue M_k of the displayed contract although α ≠ 0, changes its gap to 2M_k − δ and leaves the effective body contract unchanged; exchange of a and b is a symmetry

Equal parameters of the two types (all conditions hold, (8.12) and (8.15) vanish) and the special case ρ_T = 1, sin²p₀ = 0.01: the expansion (8.14) gives R = 1.0049851 against the exact 1.0049876, a difference of order β⁶
